_note: DECLARED subject renumbers. Copy to docs/ledger-renumbers.json and declare your own. The entries below are EXAMPLES, not declarations: the loader reads this file only if you copy it into place, and an entry whose `was` carries no legs changes nothing (rule 3).
_why: The sequence predicate compares subjects as EXACT STRINGS and normalises nothing, deliberately: guessing at intent is how a gate starts agreeing with its author. A BOARD MIGRATION breaks that premise honestly -- an item's `intake` and `claim` carry the number it had when it was FILED while its `close` carries the number it has NOW -- so the close is refused for legs that exist three inches away under the old number. A declared map is the repair; the three derivations (arithmetic, reading the live number-map at gate time, fuzzy subject matching) were each refused on measurement. See resolved_sequence_problems in tools/ledger.py.
_occupied: THE OCCUPIED CASE IS THE MAJORITY CASE, and `was`/`evidence` alone cannot express it. A migrated number is often ALREADY HELD by a different item -- measured on this factory's board 2026-11-06: 29 of the 62 migrated items carry pre-migration rows under their NEW number that belong to another unit. There, the other unit's legs satisfy a close under the string by LEANING ON them, and no gate can catch that: all five live false closes passed verify with zero problems. So the entry ALSO declares the RANGE of row numbers that belongs to that other unit, via `prior_occupant`. See unit_view in tools/ledger.py.
_rules: Each entry maps the subject a row carries NOW to the subject it carried WHEN IT WAS FILED.
`was` and `evidence` are both required and both non-blank: a renumber names the subject it WAS and the receipt that establishes the step.
A resolution only FINDS legs that already exist under the declared prior subject. It never manufactures one: an entry whose `was` carries no legs changes nothing and the close is still refused.
Positional semantics are preserved -- the prior subject's legs must still precede the close's own index.
Chains are followed (this factory's board was migrated twice), bounded at 8 hops with a visited set.
Every resolution is PRINTED with its evidence on every pass, and the count is printed at zero too, so 'none resolved' and 'the map was not consulted' cannot read alike.
ABSENT means none. A factory that has never renumbered a board has nothing to declare.

`prior_occupant` is OPTIONAL and answers a DIFFERENT question from `was`: not 'what did this subject used to be called' but 'who ELSE already held this string'. Declare it when the new number was OCCUPIED at the moment the item was renumbered.

Its `board` and `ceiling` are REQUIRED positive integers; `floor` is optional. Rows whose `n` falls inside `floor..ceiling` belong to the prior occupant and are neither legs nor blockers of the reissued unit. Omit `floor` when the prior occupant's block is a PREFIX of the subject's rows, which is the common shape.

`floor` is not inferrable. Declare it when the reissued unit files under the NEW subject BELOW the prior occupant's block; on a prefix block it is inert and may be omitted. A reissued unit's legs that carry the OLD subject are never affected by this range -- they reach the close through the declared hop, not through the partition.

ABSENT `prior_occupant` means the new number was FREE when the renumber happened. PRESENT but malformed is a typed refusal, never a silent fall back to 'free': the two readings differ by another unit's close.

#888.evidence: docs/board-migration/number-map.json: "124": {"new": 888} -- the migration that moved every service item onto a new number. OCCUPIED-NUMBER SHAPE: the string #888 was already held by the item now at board #77, whose rows under #888 are n=200..204.
